paragraphs.text: He is a megagenius scientist whose alcoholism and reckless, nihilistic behavior are sources of concern for "his daughter's" family, as well as the safety of her son, Morty.

Rick began his journey as a young inventor in Dimension C-137, where he lived with his wife Diane and daughter Beth. As Rick repeatedly failed to create interdimensional portal travel, Rick Prime, an alternate version of himself, visited Dimension C-137 and offered Rick the tools to make it possible. When Rick turned down the offer, Rick Prime, feeling insulted, responded by murdering Diane and Beth. This motivated a devastated Rick to finally invent working portal technology, becoming the only version of himself aside from Rick Prime to do so independently. He quickly utilized his new invention by going on a lifetime hunt for Rick Prime with the intent to avenge his family. At an unknown point after this, Rick Prime punished Rick for his relentless pursuit by erasing Diane Sanchez from every single reality across the Multiverse.

Soon after beginning his search, Rick ended up joining the Resistance alongside Birdperson, and later, Squanchy, where they fought against the Galactic Federation. Following the Battle of Blood Ridge, Rick left to resume looking for Rick Prime and began killing countless amounts of his alternate selves in the process over the next few decades. Eventually, the other Ricks surrendered to Rick C-137, who formed the Council of Ricks and oversaw the construction of the Citadel of Ricks, although he left before it was completed. Rick, now an elderly man, landed in Rick Prime's original dimension, taking his place as the father of that dimension's Beth Smith, hoping one day Rick Prime would return. Whilst living in the Prime Dimension, Rick formed a bond with Morty, his new grandson, and began taking him on various misadventures.

Rick would finally get his revenge when he killed Rick Prime via an unlikely alliance with Evil Morty. With his main goal in life now complete, Rick initially fell back into his alcoholic and depressive ways until Morty helped him find a new purpose in their classic adventures. Rick was also able to move on from the loss of Diane by erasing his memories of her and allowing sentient memories of her and a younger version of himself live together in harmony.

It wasn't until "Rickmurai Jack" where Rick's past is finally shown in great detail. The 'totally fabricated' backstory shown in "The Rickshank Rickdemption" was mostly based on the truth and further hinted at in "Rickternal Friendshine of the Spotless Mort".

As an adult, he married a woman named Diane and they had a daughter named Beth. Rick eventually became a scientist who was struggling to invent teleportation. One day, he was visited by an alternate version of himself, who offered him the ability to travel to different realities, but Rick refused. Insulted by what he perceived as a lesser version of himself acting as though he was better, Rick Prime sent a bomb through a portal to kill Rick C-137's Diane and Beth. Rick grieved for an unknown period of time, before inventing his own portal gun and going on a quest for revenge. As more and more Ricks began hunting Prime for the same reason, Prime invented the Omega Device, throwing in a version of Diane to wipe out their wife across existence.

Rick would spend the next few decades searching for the Rick who murdered his family. He eventually became a weapons dealer, trying to find parts for a device to help him track down the one who killed his family. Rick eventually met Birdperson at a festival, and formed a rock band called "The Flesh Curtains" together with Squanchy. The three eventually formed the core of the resistance against the Galactic Federation, culminating in the Battle of Blood Ridge. After winning the battle, Rick offered Birdperson the chance to join him in his adventures throughout the multiverse, but Birdperson refused. Hurt by this, Rick left to continue his quest for revenge.

During this time, Rick murdered several of his alternate selves, all of which belonged to an unknown organization of Ricks, yet none of them were the Rick he was searching for. At this point, Rick had become depressed after failing to find his family's murderer and often used alcohol to numb his constant mental anguish.

paragraphs.text: Morty is Rick Sanchez's grandson and often tags along on his various misadventures as a sidekick whilst attending Harry Herpson High School along with his sister, Summer.

Morty began as an incredibly anxious and submissive teenage boy who was believed to have low intelligence by those around him. He had little say in the adventures he went on with Rick and was often forced into participating, leading to Morty becoming a nervous wreck after experiencing many traumas, including the total destruction of his home dimension. However, as time passed, Morty gradually gained confidence and became a more independent person rather than a mere sidekick to Rick. This newfound confidence not only made Morty more capable, but also allowed him to occasionally distance himself from Rick and his nefarious actions, although Morty still chooses to stand by Rick whenever necessary.

It has since been revealed in "Rickmurai Jack" and "Solaricks" that Rick (C-137) is not Morty's true grandfather, as Morty is actually the biological grandson of Rick Prime, a version of Rick who murdered C-137's family.

Currently, Morty is 14 years old. He first met his grandfather, Rick Sanchez, when the latter moved into his home after supposedly being absent for 20 years. Unbeknownst to all at the time, the Rick who returned was not Morty's actual grandfather, but the Rick from Dimension C-137 and, after decades of seeking revenge for the loss of his wife and daughter while exploring the multiverse, he eventually moved into Morty's dimension, hoping that one day, Rick Prime would return to his universe so C-137 could take his revenge. Rick appeared to arrive sometime around Morty's thirteenth birthday, as Rick was present for the party. Rick eventually began wiping Morty's memories of some of their adventures, partly to keep Morty from going insane.By Rick's admission, their initial association was purely so Morty could serve as bait for Rick Prime.
Rick later states Morty's low intelligence masks Rick's high intelligence, acting as a camouflage that prevents Rick's incredible intelligence from being tracked.

Roughly six months after Rick had first met Morty, an insecure Morty asked Rick to create some kind of love potion so Jessica would fall in love with him, an annoyed Rick doing just that. As Jessica had the flu though, this created a contagion where everyone, save those genetically related to Morty, was in love with Morty. Rick attempted to cure this serum through a combination of various animal DNAs only to wind up mutating the planet into Cronenbergs. Unwilling to fix the problem, Rick decided that they should simply leave, abandoning Morty's universe for a new one. Traumatized by the affair, Morty initially kept this fact a secret only to let Summer C-131 in on it when she was suffering from an emotional crisis.

After being ambushed by the Galactic Federation at Birdperson and Tammy Guterman's wedding, the family hid on Dwarf Terrace-9, Rick leaving to "get ice cream". Understanding that Rick was sacrificing his freedom for the family's safety, Morty tried to make the best of the Federation's rule of Earth, hoping his family could have a normal life. When Summer grew desperate to save Rick, she dug Rick C-131's Portal Gun out from the backyard. To prove his point, Morty opened a portal back to the Prime Dimension, showing how Rick had callously abandoned Morty's original family. When said original family destroyed C-131's Portal Gun, guards from the Citadel responded, freezing the Prime family and taking Morty and Summer prisoner. When tried by the Council of Ricks, Morty denied renouncing Rick, warning the Council that he would come for them, a fact proven true seconds later when Rick C-137 teleported the Citadel into the Federation Prison's. After rescuing Morty and Summer, Rick brought down the Federation. Upon returning to Earth, Rick triumphantly revealed to Morty that he'd manipulated everything to have Beth divorce Jerry and make himself the dominant figure in the family and Morty's life.
Concerned about his father though, Morty guilted Rick into taking Jerry on an adventure.
Morty eventually helped himself to the Portal Gun, using it to repair Rick's damage across the galaxy only for Rick to discover what he'd done, causing the two to fall out.
She is a member of the Smith Family and the daughter of Jerry Smith and Beth Smith/Space Beth, the older sister of Morty Smith, and the mother of Naruto Smith.

She currently acts as the older sister and the granddaughter of Morty and Rick, respectively, from the Prime Dimension and Dimension C-137. For a time, she was the only other known member of the the Smith Family to be aware of that fact.
She and Morty often squabble and compete for Rick's affection, but also maintain a unique bond stemming from the revelation that the Morty she's with is not her original brother.

Summer is a female teenager of average height, thin build, and wide hips. She has a fair complexion, shoulder-length ginger hair, an oblong-shaped face, and a pointed nose. Her most common outfit has been a bright pink tank-top, white capri-pants, and black slip-on shoes. She usually has her hair pulled back in a ponytail. Notably, she shares the exact same face as her father, Jerry.
Her pajamas consist of a white under and pink shorts more often than a pink tank top with red and white striped sweatpants.

Summer has some personality traits of a typical American teenager, as she wishes to be popular among her peers, and finds the antics of her family to be dysfunctional, though she still cares for them. She's very attached to her phone and social media, taking videos of her dog Snuffles when he became super-smart, and shuddering at the thought of her father Jerry joining Facebook.

It is revealed that Summer can be jealous of the close relationship about her grandfather Rick and her brother Morty, and she can sometimes feel ignored by her grandfather. While Rick tries to keep her at a distance, the two of them have gone on their own adventures, including on the planet Gazorpazorp. Her complex of being ignored by Rick exhibits into a connection with the Devil in "Something Ricked This Way Comes".

Although Summer is not as scientifically-minded as her grandfather Rick, she does possess intelligence. Summer is shown to be a very smart and nimble-witted teen, at least compared to rest of her family. Currently, she is not as violent as Beth was when Beth was young, but enjoys fighting alongside Rick and reacts quickly to life-or-death situations.

She is also a sociopathic and narcissistic person, like her grandfather; similar to the way that Morty responds, but only when truly pushed to his limits. Summer, however, seems more readily able to access these elements of her deeper-rooted personality when subjected to her grandfather Rick's influence for a relatively short amount of time, as seen in "Rickmancing the Stone".

She is also shown to possess a strong desire for family. Her stance towards them is best summarized in her quote from "The Wedding Squanchers", where she explains that she would rather live an isolated existence without a future if it means that the family won't have to abandon Rick, saying that she believes that, "you don't love someone in hopes of a reward". In "The Rickchurian Mortydate", she is shown to reiterate this sentiment when she freely runs away with the family to a cabin in the woods so that Beth will never have to experience her existential crisis alone.

Summer seems jealous of the fact that her grandfather Rick chooses to go on adventures with her brother Morty and not her. Rick claims that the opinions of his granddaughter Summer mean "very little" to him, but he still cares for her, as he admits that the top Summer wears in "Raising Gazorpazorp" is cute.

Summer gets a part-time job at a cursed antique store run by the Devil, aka Mr. Needful, just to spite Rick, in "Something Ricked This Way Comes". Despite this, Rick helps his granddaughter Summer buff up and take revenge on Mr. Needful after they get fired by him. Afterwards, the two go around beating up other people doing bad things.

In "Ricksy Business", Summer, along with her brother and grandfather, freezes time to stop her parents from finding their house in wretched shape. She proceeds to have fun together all around town, doing things like carving pumpkins, pulling peoples' pants down, and watching the movie Titanic together.

She is the daughter of Rick C-131 (deceased) and Diane Sanchez C-131, the wife of Jerry Smith (originally of Jerry Smith C-131), and the mother of Summer Smith and the deceased Morty Smith (C-131). She currently acts as the mother of Morty Smith of the Prime Dimension and the daughter of the Rick Sanchez of Dimension C-137, respectively. She also works as a veterinarian at the St. Equis Hospital.

Characterized by a superiority complex and abandonment issues, Beth gradually came to struggle with her husband over his contributions to their marriage, due in part to his lower-level position and subsequent employment, further driven by her father influencing her feelings of superiority.

Around the same time, Beth grappled with the decision to leave her family in order to find herself or stay on Earth and accept things for the way they are. She ended up leaving Rick to decide for her, who created a clone of Beth and mixed the two around so not even he would know which one was the original Beth. One of the Beths flew out into space, whilst the other remained on Earth beside her family.

The details of Beth's history are relatively unknown; she was born from Rick Sanchez and Diane Sanchez (C-131), and she has recounted herself as a "bright-eyed" woman from Muskegon, Michigan in "Meeseeks and Destroy." As indicated in "Hot Rick" during Beth's childhood, her parents' marriage deteriorated amid unknown circumstances, and Rick decided to leave both Beth and her mother to travel across the cosmos. Beth blamed herself for her parents falling out, and seeing her father as an intelligent scientist compared to her mother, Beth came to idolize Rick and blamed Diane for "chasing off the dad with the guts to leave".

It is revealed in "The ABC's of Beth" that, at some point in her childhood, Beth became an insane and psychotic little girl. She began asking her father, Rick, to create toy-like weapons for her so she can harm other children. As an adult, Beth reasoned that she did that to "spend time with her father." Rick, aware of the increasing danger that would represent his daughter, created a dream world, Froopyland, for her in order to keep the other children of the neighborhood safe. Beth managed to take one of her friends, Tommy, to Froopyland, where, according to Tommy himself, she pushed him into a honey swamp as she was envious of the good relationship he has with his father. Then, she convinced herself that Tommy only got lost in Froopyland and therefore went missing.

Beth was somewhat distant towards her children at their childhood, as implied in "Raising Gazorpazorp." Her job as a veterinary surgeon at St. Equis Hospital causes her to spend less time with her husband and children, and she feels that coddling them would make them dependent or end up like her husband.
Sometime after "The ABC's of Beth," Rick cloned her, resulting in two Beths. It is unknown which Beth is the original and which one is the clone.

Beth is a slender, pale fair-skinned woman of above average height with an oval-shaped face and slightly wavy shoulder-length blonde hair in a long bob cut, she also has a big bust. She wears berry pink-colored lipstick for makeup, has a pointed nose, and long eyelashes. She wears a short-sleeve V-neck collared desire-red polo shirt, straight-leg blue pants and slip-on white shoes. Beth admits that, since her unwanted pregnancy, her waistline has widened.

As a little girl, Beth wore a short-sleeve light red shirt with light blue shortalls, calf-length white frilly socks, and periwinkle Mary Jane shoes. She wears a white and light blue hair clip, two blue and green wristbands on her right wrist.

Beth is an intelligent, ambitious, and independent woman who suffers from a variety of deep-seated insecurities. A dedicated veterinary horse surgeon, she is the family's main breadwinner and often tries to do the best for her family based on this sense of responsibility. She is highly insecure about her profession as a horse surgeon, and is quick to snap at the implication she is not a 'real' surgeon or a 'real' veterinarian. She may share this belief, wishing she had been able to continue her medical education to become a 'real' doctor in Rixty Minutes.
Jerry is the husband of Beth Smith, the father of Summer Smith and Morty Smith, and the son-in-law of Rick Sanchez.

Jerry is often noted as somewhat of a loser. He is most often characterized as struggling with employment and failing to connect with his family. However, he is capable of heroism in times of crisis and has saved his family's lives on several occasions.

Jerry also has an adversarial relationship with his father-in-law, Rick and he often competes with the latter for the admiration of his family. However, that hasn't stopped Jerry from becoming more involved in Rick's space adventures.

Jerry is the husband of Beth Smith, the father of Summer Smith and Morty Smith, and the son-in-law of Rick Sanchez and Diane Sanchez. He is also the son of Leonard Smith and Joyce Smith, the nephew of an unnamed man, and the grandson of Nana and Pop-Pop. He currently acts as the father and the son-in-law of Morty Smith from Prime Dimension and Rick Sanchez from Dimension C-137, respectively. The same goes for Beth and Summer. He acts as the father of Summer Smith from Dimension C-131 and as the husband of Beth Smith from the same dimension.

Jerry always tries to think of the best interest of the family, but his attempt to be the patriarch of the family can often be misguided by his self-centered nature. This causes him a great deal of conflict with Rick, as his father-in-law clearly has no respect for him whatsoever.

He was staying at the Jerryboree and was accidentally switched with Jerry Smith from Dimension C-131 before being taken home by Rick and Morty. This wouldn't be revealed until "Solaricks" when Jerry was sent back to his home dimension, before being rescued by Rick.

Jerry Smith (5126) was born to Joyce and Leonard Smith in the Dimension 5126. He met Beth 5126 in high school. When she was 17, Jerry accidentally got her pregnant. They got married and had a daughter, Summer 5126, followed three years later by a son, Morty 5126. Their marriage was complicated, but they lived together nonetheless.

One day, Rick C-137 was teaching Morty Prime how to fly the Space Cruiser. Jerry C-131 was with them, but Rick hadn't noticed him. Upon spotting his son-in-law, he flew into a rage and took Jerry to Jerryboree—a daycare for alternate versions of Jerry. There, Jerry C-131 spent the entire day getting to know other Jerrys. Later, Rick and Morty returned to the daycare to pick up Jerry. However, Morty had lost the claim ticket, making it impossible to verify if the Jerry there was theirs; consequently, Rick Sanchez (5126) proposed swapping Jerry C-131 for Jerry 5126. From that point on, Jerry 5126 became the Jerry—a member of the Smith family—while Jerry C-131 became a member of the 5126 Smith Family.

After the Galactic Federation took over Earth in "The Wedding Squanchers", the travelers were forced to leave the planet. Consequently, Jerry secured a job with the Galactic Federation and earned a measure of respect from Beth—placing him in her favor over Rick. Afterward, he returned to his family. As a result, Jerry lost his job and issued an ultimatum to Beth: it was either him or Rick. She chose her father by proxy, which led to her divorce from Jerry.

For the first time in a long while, he encountered his original family. Given the nature of the relationship they had with Jerry C-131, they treated their own original Jerry with hatred. This made him feel uncomfortable, until the Smith family returned for him. Following that, he left his home dimension.

He is of European-American descent. Jerry has a medium complexion and has scruffy, dirty brown hair, with slight curls. He has dimples and wears a dark green shirt, with a brown and beige stripe in the middle. He also wears light blue long pants and black shoes. Notably, he shares the exact same face with his daughter, Summer. At 5'10" (1.78 m), he is the second tallest member of the Smith-Sanchez family, behind Rick.

Though because of those around him, and by comparison to other, less than ordinary characters, is commonly relegated to less than a punchline, being often viewed by other characters as an obnoxious loser, a pathetic father, and a pitiful husband.

He is one of the many versions of Morty from across the multiverse, but unique in being notably amoral, ruthless and displaying intelligence rivalling that of Rick. He initially appeared alongside Evil Rick, who was hunting down and killing several Ricks throughout the multiverse. It was later revealed Evil Rick was merely being controlled by Evil Morty, although he remained undetected and travelled to the Citadel by posing as one of the Mortys liberated from Evil Rick's lair.

He served as the first Morty to be democratically elected President of The Citadel, and had consolidated his power in a coup by eliminating any disagreeable Ricks in the Shadow Council of Ricks. He later used this rise to power to fabricate an escape from the Central Finite Curve, destroying almost the entire Citadel and killing countless Ricks and Mortys in the process. Despite his hope to be rid of Rick once and for all, he finds himself dragged into Rick C-137 and Morty Prime's circle of influence, reluctantly cooperating with them as they face off against the bigger existential threat of Rick Prime and the Omega Device.

Evil Morty assisted Rick C-137 in taking down Rick Prime, and stole the plans for the Omega Device in the process. He left after warning Rick to leave him alone, lest he use the Omega Device to end the "Rick experiment" once and for all. He later returned to blackmail Rick into helping with his plans until Rick destroys his version of the Omega Device, ensuing a fierce battle. Evil Morty uses a time device he reverse engineered from Rick's time travel box to freeze time, gloating that he is willing to use time travel unlike Ricks. However, the Time Cops arrive and arrest Evil Morty for messing with time, which was Rick's plan all along as he knew Evil Morty would be cocky enough to mess with time. Evil Morty is then sent to an unknown time prison.

As revealed in "Unmortricken", Evil Morty was once another Morty, constantly mistreated and dragged on adventures. One day, he grew fed up with his Rick and got him blackout drunk while he engineered a device that would allow him to control Rick, to be hidden underneath a black eyepatch. He scalped him and attached the device to his brain. After that, Evil Morty teleported to the Morty Agency in the Citadel, killed the employees and erased himself from the database. Apparently, his original goal was to destroy the rule of Ricks. He built/occupied the base of operations on the planet Crustula and went about kidnapping Ricks and Mortys: Ricks for information about the Citadel and absorbing their knowledge and Mortys to use them as cloaking devices to hide the brain waves of his Rick from the Citadel. He eventually found out about the Central Finite Curve.

He first appears in "Close Rick-counters of the Rick Kind", where at first it appears he is simply a sidekick to Evil Rick, assisting him in killing twenty-seven known Ricks from various dimensions and capturing, torturing, and enslaving hundreds of Mortys to use them as cloaking devices to hide from the Citadel. Earlier Evil Morty hacked Rick C-137's portal gun and uploaded his own portal travel history and sent it to the Citadel authorities to frame C-137 so they could arrest him for killing and kidnapping of Ricks and Mortys. Then Rick C-137 escaped and found out the source of the hack to go to Evil Morty's controlled territory by getting caught. Evil Morty downloaded Rick C-137's brain and found out that he created the Central Finite Curve. To escape it he needed to get access to all the resources of the Citadel.

A year later, in "The Ricklantis Mixup," now going by the alias "Candidate Morty" (survived the Citadel battle in "The Rickshank Rickdemption" or was absent from the Citadel at that time), he secretly develops an alter-ego to become a presidential candidate in an election for the newly democratic Citadel of Ricks. His candidacy is considered a joke by the Ricks of the Citadel due to being a Morty who no one takes seriously, including his Campaign Manager Morty. But, after making a rousing speech about the class divide between the various Ricks and Mortys on the Citadel during the debate, he quickly earned praise and support.

paragraphs.text: He was the Rick who was responsible for the deaths of Diane in every single dimension, and Beth Sanchez in Dimension C-137. Rick C-137 attempted to find and kill Rick Prime throughout the multiverse for decades, killing countless other Ricks in the process.
In "Solaricks", Rick C-137 resets portal travelers, thereby sending Rick Prime back to his original dimension. Rick Prime then encounters Jerry Prime and kills him.

In "Unmortricken", it is revealed that Rick Prime invented a weapon known to inferiors as the Omega Device (though Rick Prime claims that the device is "too cool for a name" and inferiors meaning lesser ricks, ie, ones who didn't invent portal travel on their own, but ones who just took it from others who actually did, such as Rick Prime and Rick C-137), which has the power to erase an individual from every dimension, as well as interfere with other people's memories of that individual. Rick C-137 and Evil Morty temporarily join forces, and managed to track down Rick Prime. They engage him in a vicious fight, which they barely win. Evil Morty then steals Rick Prime's schematics for the Omega Device before giving Rick C-137 the opportunity to kill his nemesis. Rick Prime, defiant to the end, ceaselessly mocks Rick for becoming like him as he is slowly beaten to death.

Following Rick Prime's death, Rick C-137 briefly became depressed, as he no longer had a goal now that his nemesis was dead. However, Morty intervened and encouraged Rick to resume their regular adventures. Rick Prime's legacy briefly lived on with Evil Morty, who took the plans for the Omega Device and used them to threaten Rick C-137, lest he put an end to the "Rick experiment", before Rick C-137 took advantage of Evil Morty's complacency and used the Omega Device on its own blueprints, wiping out the weapon forevermore.

Rick Prime had more grayish skin than other versions of Ricks, as well as more dull-colored hair in a "nondescript" haircut. He wore a purplish "sci-fi" jacket with a gray shoulder pad and a red shirt underneath. After many years, his appearance was completely unchanged, implying that he either transferred his mind to a cloned body or his healing abilities also give him longevity.

Rick C-137 refers to Rick Prime as "the real deal" to Morty Prime. His reasoning for this is that Rick Prime was a narcissist who actively hated attachments to his family to the point that he was willing to abandon them for over 20 years. Rick Prime also believed other Ricks should follow suit, leading him to murder Beth and Diane from Dimension C-137, thus doing away with Rick C-137's attachments in that world. When certain Ricks defied him, he decided to teach them a lesson by committing the deplorable act of wiping out all versions of Diane across the multiverse.

Being a Rick, he shares all of his counterpart's intellect and resourcefulness, though he does not seem to indulge in any hedonistic acts like drinking or partying. It is possible Rick Prime is somewhat more intelligent than most other Ricks, as he states that he and Rick C-137 are the only Ricks to ever figure out inter-dimensional portal travel on their own. (All other Ricks having been gifted the technology by Prime himself, or other Ricks whom Prime gave it to.) Like most Ricks though, Prime shows signs of hypocrisy, being willing to kill his original Morty, yet acting shocked when Evil Morty, whom he mistook for his biological grandson, attacked him.

In a sense, Rick Prime's personality is what Rick pretended to be for years, a self-absorbed man who didn't care about anyone, upholding the nihilistic philosophy that all other Ricks project. Despite this, he does appear to have some affection for his family. He held some fondness for Slow Mobius, saying that killing him would hurt and having a look of sorrow when he subjected Slow Mobius to the Omega Device. When he thought he met his original Morty, actually Evil Morty, he attempted to make small talk before killing him and later praised Evil Morty's ruthless nature, even attempting an alliance. He also appeared outraged that Rick C-137 had lived in his house with his daughter and grandson.

At the end of "The ABC's of Beth", Beth had a revelation about herself and Rick gave her the opportunity to go out into the universe and see where it takes her. He offered to make a clone of her with all her memories to take over her life on earth until she returned. Beth asked him to decide, whether or not he wanted his daughter in his life. Unable to decide, he went ahead and made the clone, labeled "Clone Beth". He put both Beths in sleep pods, then purposefully removed the labels on the pods and had their positions shuffled so that he himself would not know which Beth was the clone. He sent one Beth out into space and kept the other at home. He wiped his own memory of the incident (later, this leads him to finally admit to himself that he is a terrible father).

During her adventures in space, Space Beth joined a vigilante group called The Defiance, who were waging war against the Gromflomites and were working to stop them from reestablishing the Galactic Federation.

By the time of "Star Mort Rickturn of the Jerri", Space Beth has gone on several space adventures to reach the most wanted status. A Defiance Doctor discovers a chip implanted in her neck that will seemingly kill her should she return to Earth and get in proximity of the other Beth. She removed the chip and returns to Earth to murder Rick for lying to her, as well as the other Beth, but Rick makes her see the other Beth has a chip too. According to Rick, the other Beth's chip would have transferred a copy of her memories to Space Beth before vaporizing her. She relents and Rick invites her to lunch after they are shown equal in gadgets. She talks with him, surprised the other Beth is still with Jerry before they come under attack, during which, Rick inadvertently implies Space Beth may be the actual clone. Space Beth tracks down her father and counterpart who wanted to talk with her, causing a crash. Space Beth catches up and nearly succeeds in killing her before they are kidnapped by Tammy. While incarcerated, they talk about their contrasting lives and they reach common ground. Working together, the two versions of Beth defeat the aliens and both come to help Rick with Phoenixperson, and they both are impressed with Jerry coming in handy. Space Beth also meets Summer and Morty who are amazed to have two versions of their mother. At the end, it is revealed Rick doesn't know which Beth is which, as he erased his own memory. However, the two versions of Beth and wider Smith family are content with the mystery, as they now respect one another and are unwilling to give Rick any sense of satisfaction.

In "Mortyplicity", Space Beth returned to space and bumped into her family along the way, before returning home with them. Rick commented that may happen more often, something Space Beth politely declined on. After Rick discovered his decoy families went rogue, Space Beth and the other Beth question this.

In "Solaricks", Space Beth rescues Rick and Morty and brings them back to Earth, and is pressed to stick around with the family by Summer. She, Summer and Beth are sent to the Citadel to loot and fight scavengers but playing a role in bringing the family back together, but Summer's favouritism towards Space Beth drives jealousy between her and Beth. They argue until they are consumed by a monster, then apologize, with Space Beth expressing her lack of interest in anyone's approval. Summer then exasperatingly scolds them both, she expresses that she would want Space Beth to be around more like a mother, and admits later her favouritism is fleeting and not to worry about it so much. Due to the Earth being frundled, Space Beth and the rest of the family are forced to relocate to another dimension. She buries the native Space Beth in the backyard, as the other family members bury their respective counterparts. After more apologies to Beth, before Space Beth suggests boundaries are good while admitting she would like to relax her own.

paragraphs.text: He and Tammy later get married, only for Tammy to reveal herself as a Galactic Federation agent out to kill Birdperson, arrest Rick, and all of his associates. Despite being shot multiple times, Birdperson is soon resurrected by the Federation as the cyborg Phoenixperson in order to serve them. In "Star Mort: Rickturn of the Jerri", Phoenixperson - under the control of the Galactic Federation - comes face to face with Rick, and fights him, almost killing him, before being shut down by Space Beth.

Following the destruction of the federation, Phoenixperson was salvaged by the Smith family and resided in Rick's garage lab, until Rick restored him to normal. Birdperson then discovered he had a daughter with Tammy and went to search for her.

Rick-C137 and Memory Rick eavesdrop on a meeting between Resistance fighters where a Grapflapian says, "Some of us still have home planets to protect," to which Birdperson responds, "And some of us do not. We need to fight. The impassive is incapable of mercy." Altogether, this seems to imply that Birdperson's home planet was destroyed by the Federation (likely via the infection shown that causes glowing red eyes and a loss of reason in Birdpeople), which is why he joined the Freedom Fighters.
He is also one of the very few party-goers who remains behind to help clean up, although he may have just been waiting for Tammy to be ready to leave.

When Morty shows his frustration at the party's mess as it would mean no more adventures with Rick if his parents see the house in this state, Birdperson informs Morty that "Wubba lubba dub dub" means "I am in great pain, please help me" in his native language. Morty is skeptical that Rick actually means this, though this knowledge spurs him to eventually press Rick into action to preserve their ability to go on adventures together.

He explains to Morty that leaving Rick was a "dick move", and that Rick really does care about him. Furthermore, if it wasn't for Rick, he [Birdperson] would be dead and would never have met Morty. He then recharges the Portal gun and sends Morty back to Rick.

In "Get Schwifty," it can be noted that Birdperson and Rick have been acquainted for years, as there are many picture frames containing Rick on his wall. During Birdperson's early adulthood, he, Rick and Squanchy formed a band called "The Flesh Curtains", where Birdperson was featured as the main singer. Birdperson can also be seen beside a younger Rick, and some sort of aircraft.

In "The Wedding Squanchers", he and Tammy get married and have a huge wedding party. During this time, he confessed to Beth that he and Rick are wanted by the Galactic Federation for committing "crimes in the name of freedom" which Beth shrugs off. Shortly after, during the reception, Tammy reveals herself to be a member of the Galactic Federation's secret service and shoots Birdperson multiple times, followed by a shootout with the rest of the criminals in the room.

Tammy and the Gromflomites resurrected Birdperson as a cyborg and renamed him Phoenixperson. Although Tammy wanted his name to be Cyberbird, she didn't push hard enough to make that official. She settled on Phoenixperson and took off with him.

In "Star Mort Rickturn of the Jerri", Rick came face to face with Phoenixperson where they briefly talked and started fighting as soon as Rick said that he killed Tammy. Phoenixperson flew into a rage and fought Rick to death. During their fight, Rick mentioned how he wondered who would win in a fight between them, to which Phoenixperson replied that Rick was "always a bad friend." The fight seemed to gain in favor of Phoenixperson, as Rick was suffering from massive injuries to the point where his cyber-augmented intestines spilled out. Just before Rick was about to accept his death, the fight was interrupted by both Beth and her counterpart Space Beth. However, Phoenixperson ended the fight quickly. Just before he could kill Rick, Jerry (equipped with the invisible belt) used Tammy's corpse to pretend that she was still alive. Phoenixperson was surprised but was suspicious by how she was acting. Jerry then tripped on top of the corpse, accidentally uncloaking himself.

paragraphs.text: Squanchy is a cat-like anthropomorphic creature, who is a very close friend of Rick and Birdperson. He appears to share Rick's love for alcohol and partying.

It has been shown Squanchy once fought alongside Rick and Birdperson in a rebellion against the Galactic Federation. This would later come back to hurt the trio, as they were ambushed at Birdperson's wedding several decades later. Squanchy transformed into his berserker form and fought off the Federation army whilst Rick escaped with his family. He ultimately survived the encounter and returned to living peacefully on his home planet.

In "The Wedding Squanchers", after Tammy reveals herself as a deep cover agent for the Galactic Federation and the wedding reception is ambushed by Gromflomites, Squanchy tells Rick to save his family and get out of there before pulling out one of his teeth and breaking it in half to consume a green liquid substance, which subsequently turns him into a giant version of himself with superhuman strength and endurance.

However, when Rick is mining Death Crystals in "Edge of Tomorty: Rick Die Rickpeat", one of his possible deaths is being ripped in half by Squanchy in his berserker form. This future could have only been a possibility if Squanchy survived his fight with Tammy. This is later confirmed to be true, as Squanchy returns in "How Poopy Got His Poop Back" and Rick directly comments on him surviving the battle at the wedding.

He is first seen participating in The Battle of Blood Ridge with Rick and Birdperson as apart of the Freedom Fighters Crew. He is later seen attending Geardude's funeral and mourning over him as Rick mentions him having a distasteful eulogy. He is also seen performing stand-up at a bar during his terrible stand-up phase which Rick and Birdperson attend. He is again seen at the Birding Manapalooza Flargabarg as he, Rick, and Birdperson go on stage to perform and form The Flesh Curtains.

After gathering the group fully, they all go to a bar called F#%k You's, where they begin drinking and partying instead. Afterwards they party and go to several other locations, they meet Hugh Jackman and party at his house. After deciding that he and the others are going to find Mr. Poopybutthole's ex-wife Amy, Squanchy and the others proceed to her house, where they discover she is having an affair with a Predator private investigator named Gul'Karna, who begins hunting and attacking them. During their confrontation with the Predator, Squanchy pulls out a tooth and consumes the green liquid substance in order to become his giant self but is unable to do so properly due to being drunk. After Mr. Poopybutthole's situation is resolved, Squanchy takes a "fading pill" and checked himself into rehab. However, he did not stick with it and was later arrested for smuggling toad venom across the border.

Squanchy is a short orange cat-person with a tiny blue nose, a dark brown goatee, messy fur and whiskers. He has a naked tail with a brown tuft of hair on its tip. When he drinks the green liquid from his tooth, he becomes a big, muscular cat-person with green eyes, a larger beard, vast tufts of hair on his giant shoulders, black claws, and sharper teeth.
He appears to a good friend of Rick's. Personality-wise, he is a party animal who behaves very wildly.

He is also a very loyal friend of Rick and Birdperson, as when the Galactic Federation crashes Birdperson's wedding and winds up mortally injuring Birdperson, Squanchy tells Rick to escape with his family whilst he would remain and fight off the Federation forces. Whilst Squanchy was eventually revealed to have survived this battle, this shows he was willing to die to protect his friends. Before the battle, despite his loyalty to Rick, he was shown to be disappointed by Rick calling Birdperson his best friend. Squanchy responded by removing a friendship bracelet inscribed with "Rick's BFF".

Squanchy also has a habit to replace most of his verbs with the term "squanch" as it is native to his species' dialect, much like how the Smurfs say "smurf" instead of certain words. Beth draws this comparison upon meeting him for the first time at Birdperson's wedding.
